description: Camp two was the bedrock — solid ground, always true. Camp three is the ground you've already crossed. Past simple describes finished actions: tents…

hero.lede: Camp two was the bedrock — solid ground, always true. Camp three is the ground you've already crossed. Past simple describes finished actions: tents struck, terrain covered, a chapter closed off from where you're standing now.

cards.head: A completed action
cards.body: One finished event at a specific point in the past.

cards.head: A past habit or routine
cards.body: Something you regularly did, but no longer do.
cards.ex: "We climbed every weekend when we lived in the Alps."

cards.head: A sequence of events
cards.body: Telling a story: one thing happened, then the next.
cards.ex: "She packed her bag, closed the door, and left."

cards.head: A historical fact
cards.body: Something true for a period that has since ended.

cards.head: A past state or feeling
cards.body: A condition or opinion that no longer applies.
cards.ex: "I didn't like coffee when I was a child."

cards.head: A specific past moment
cards.body: Anchored to a stated or clearly implied time.

cards.head: Affirmative
cards.body: subject + past form (regular: base + -ed · irregular: its own form)

cards.head: Wh- questions
cards.body: question word + did + subject + base verb?

charts.head: Conjugation chart
charts.note: The regular pattern doesn't change by person — using the verb "to work" as the model. Irregular verbs (go → went, see → saw, have → had) have to be learned individually.

charts.head: The verb "to be" in the past
charts.note: The one verb that doesn't use did — it conjugates directly, with only two forms.

signals.head: Finished time markers
items: two days ago / a year ago

panels.head: Now — open
items: I am finishing the report right now.

quiz.hint: A regular verb, one completed action.
quiz.explain: A single completed past action takes the regular past simple ending -ed: finished.
Go is irregular: go → went. "Goed" doesn't exist, and "gone" is a past participle, used with have.

quiz.prompt: We _____ a wonderful time at the festival. (have)
quiz.explain: Have is irregular in the past: have → had.

quiz.hint: Negative form: did + not + base verb.
quiz.explain: The negative past simple is subject + didn't + base verb: didn't meet. The main verb stays in its base form — "didn't met" is a common error.

quiz.prompt: She _____ the message before she left. (not / receive)
quiz.explain: didn't + base verb: didn't receive, never didn't + past form.

quiz.hint: Yes/No question: Did + subject + base verb?
quiz.explain: Yes/No questions in past simple use Did + subject + base verb: Did you hear?

quiz.prompt: Where _____ you _____ your holiday last year? (spend)
quiz.hint: Wh- question: question word + did + subject + base verb?
quiz.explain: Wh- questions follow question word + did + subject + base verb: Where did you spend?

quiz.prompt: It _____ raining heavily when we left the house. (be)
quiz.hint: The verb "to be" in the past — singular subject.
quiz.explain: "It" is singular, so the past of be is was.

quiz.prompt: They _____ ready when the taxi arrived. (not / be)
quiz.explain: "They" is plural, so the negative past of be is weren't. "Didn't be" is never correct — be doesn't use did.

quiz.hint: A question with "to be" doesn't need did.
quiz.explain: Questions with be invert the subject and verb directly: Were you...? No did is needed.

quiz.prompt: The car _____ suddenly at the junction. (stop)
quiz.hint: Spelling rule: short vowel + single consonant doubles.
quiz.explain: One-syllable verbs ending consonant-vowel-consonant double the final letter before -ed: stop → stopped.

quiz.prompt: He _____ hard and passed the exam. (study)
quiz.hint: Spelling rule: consonant + y changes to i before -ed.
quiz.explain: A consonant before final y changes y to i before -ed: study → studied.
See is irregular: see → saw. "Seen" is the past participle, used with have, not alone.

quiz.prompt: We arrived at the airport, checked in, and then _____ through security. (go)
quiz.hint: Third step in a sequence of past events.
quiz.explain: A sequence of finished actions in a story all stay in past simple: arrived, checked in, went.

results: Camp struck. Every step behind you accounted for.
Solid progress. A couple of loose stones to check before camp four.
Good first attempt. Worth another pass before moving on.
